# Kinematics: Most-Missed Quiz

Name: ______________________  Period: ______  Date: ____________

> The interactive version, with instant feedback, is at [quiz.html?unit=kinematics](../../quiz.html?unit=kinematics).

**1. A ball is thrown straight up. At the very top of its path, what is its acceleration?**

- A. Zero, because it has stopped
- B. 9.8 m/s² downward
- C. 9.8 m/s² upward
- D. It depends on the mass of the ball

**2. A position–time graph shows a flat horizontal line. What is the object doing?**

- A. Staying at rest
- B. Moving at constant velocity
- C. Speeding up steadily
- D. Moving backward

**3. A car has a negative acceleration. Which statement must be true?**

- A. It is slowing down
- B. It is moving backward
- C. It will stop soon
- D. Its acceleration points in the negative direction

**4. A runner completes exactly one lap of a 400 m track in 50 s. What is her average velocity?**

- A. 8 m/s
- B. 4 m/s
- C. 0 m/s
- D. 20 000 m/s

**5. On a velocity–time graph, velocity rises in a straight line from 0 to 10 m/s over 5 s. How far does the object travel?**

- A. 50 m
- B. 25 m
- C. 2 m
- D. 10 m

**6. A bowling ball and a tennis ball are dropped from the same height at the same time. Ignoring air resistance, which lands first?**

- A. They land at the same time
- B. The bowling ball
- C. The tennis ball
- D. It depends on the height

**7. A stone dropped from rest falls about 5 m in the first second. About how far has it fallen after 2 seconds?**

- A. 10 m
- B. 15 m
- C. 40 m
- D. 20 m

**8. A car braking at a constant rate needs 20 m to stop from 10 m/s. With the same braking, how far does it need to stop from 20 m/s?**

- A. 40 m
- B. 30 m
- C. 80 m
- D. 20 m

<details>
<summary>Answer key and explanations</summary>

1. **B.** Velocity is zero at the top, but gravity is still acting, so the acceleration is still 9.8 m/s² downward. If acceleration were zero the ball would stay at the top. *Common mistake: Confusing zero velocity with zero acceleration.*
2. **A.** The slope of a position–time graph is velocity. A flat line has zero slope, so the velocity is zero. (A flat line on a velocity–time graph would mean constant velocity.) *Common mistake: Mixing up position–time and velocity–time graphs.*
3. **D.** The sign only gives direction. If the car is also moving in the negative direction, a negative acceleration makes it speed up. *Common mistake: Believing negative acceleration always means slowing down.*
4. **C.** She ends where she started, so displacement is zero, and average velocity = displacement ÷ time = 0. Her average speed is 8 m/s. *Common mistake: Using distance instead of displacement.*
5. **B.** Displacement is the area under the line: a triangle with area ½ × 5 s × 10 m/s = 25 m. Multiplying 10 × 5 = 50 m treats the object as if it moved at top speed the whole time. *Common mistake: Using final velocity × time instead of the area (average velocity × time).*
6. **A.** In free fall every object has the same acceleration, 9.8 m/s², regardless of mass. *Common mistake: Believing heavier objects fall faster.*
7. **D.** Δx = ½at², so distance depends on time squared. Double the time gives four times the distance: 4 × 5 m = 20 m. *Common mistake: Assuming distance doubles when time doubles.*
8. **C.** From v² = v₀² + 2aΔx, stopping distance is proportional to v₀². Doubling the speed makes the distance four times as large. *Common mistake: Assuming stopping distance is proportional to speed.*

</details>
